article.title: Why Statistical Significance Is Not the Same as Business Value
article.why: Separate evidence of an effect from whether the effect is worth acting on.

paragraphs.en:
An A/B test can produce a statistically significant result that is still a poor business decision. Statistical significance tells us whether an observed difference is unlikely to be explained by random sampling variation under a particular model. It does not tell us whether the effect is large enough to matter economically.

Suppose a retailer tests a new message on two million customers. The treatment group has a conversion rate of 1.02 percent and control has 1.00 percent. With such a large sample, the 0.02 percentage-point difference might become statistically significant. But the practical effect is only twenty additional conversions per 100,000 customers. Whether that is valuable depends on revenue, margin, campaign cost, and operational complexity.

This is why effect size should be reported alongside p-values. A tiny effect can be estimated very precisely and still be unimportant. Conversely, a moderate effect in a small experiment may fail to reach conventional significance because the estimate is noisy. ‘Not significant’ does not automatically mean ‘no effect,’ just as ‘significant’ does not mean ‘important.’

Confidence intervals help connect uncertainty with magnitude. Instead of saying only that the p-value is below 0.05, analysts can report the estimated lift and a plausible range. If the interval contains only effects that are too small to cover campaign costs, the result may be statistically credible but economically unattractive.

Business value also depends on scale. A tiny per-customer effect can become valuable when applied cheaply to tens of millions of customers. The same effect may be worthless if each treatment requires an expensive coupon, call-center contact, or manual process. Therefore the relevant question is expected incremental profit, not significance alone.

Heterogeneity matters as well. The overall average effect may be small, while one segment shows a meaningful lift and another shows none. Targeting only the responsive segment can transform an unattractive broad campaign into a profitable one. Segment analysis should be planned carefully, however, because searching many subgroups after the fact increases the chance of finding misleading patterns.

Decision thresholds should ideally be defined before the experiment. A team can specify a minimum detectable effect for statistical planning and a minimum economically meaningful effect for business planning. These are related but different. The first concerns what the experiment can reliably detect; the second concerns what would justify action.

For example, management might decide that a campaign needs at least 0.10 percentage points of incremental conversion to cover discounts and delivery costs. If the experiment estimates a 0.03-point lift with very high statistical confidence, the correct decision may still be not to scale.

The reverse situation also deserves attention. Suppose the estimated lift is 0.15 points, but the confidence interval is wide because the sample is small. The result may be promising even if it is not yet significant. The next step could be a larger test rather than immediate rejection.

A good experiment report therefore separates four questions: Is there evidence of an effect? How large is the estimated effect? How uncertain is that estimate? Does the expected economic value justify implementation? Keeping these questions separate prevents p-values from becoming automatic go/no-go rules.

Statistical significance is useful evidence, but business decisions require a value model. The best conclusion is not ‘p < 0.05, therefore launch.’ It is ‘the estimated incremental effect, uncertainty, expected margin, and implementation cost together support or do not support scaling.’
paragraphs.zh:
A/B test 即使達到 statistical significance，也可能不是好的 business decision。Statistical significance 告訴我們觀察到的差異是否不太可能只是 sampling variation，但它不會告訴我們 effect 是否大到具有經濟意義。

例如零售商對200萬人測試新訊息，treatment conversion 1.02%，control 1.00%。因 sample 很大，0.02 percentage-point 的差可能達顯著，但實務上每10萬人只多20個 conversions。是否值得，仍取決於 revenue、margin、campaign cost 與 operational complexity。

因此 effect size 應和 p-value 一起報告。很小的 effect 可以被非常精確地估計，但仍不重要；反過來，小樣本中 moderate effect 也可能因不確定性大而未達顯著。Not significant 不等於 no effect，significant 也不等於 important。

Confidence interval 能把 uncertainty 與 magnitude 放在一起。若整個區間都小到無法 cover campaign cost，那結果即使 statistically credible，仍可能 economically unattractive。

Business value 也取決於 scale。每位顧客 effect 很小，但如果能低成本套用到幾千萬人，仍可能有價值；若每次 treatment 都需要昂貴 coupon、call center 或人工流程，同樣 effect 就可能不划算。真正相關的是 expected incremental profit。

Heterogeneity 也重要。Overall effect 可能很小，但某 segment lift 很高，另一群為零。只 target responsive segment，可能把不划算的 broad campaign 變成 profitable campaign。但 subgroup 分析要事先規劃，避免事後大量搜尋造成假訊號。

決策 threshold 最好在 experiment 前先定義。Minimum detectable effect 是統計規劃問題，minimum economically meaningful effect 是 business decision 問題。兩者不同。

例如 management 規定至少要有0.10 percentage points 的 incremental conversion 才 cover cost，而 experiment 精確估出0.03，那即使 p-value 很漂亮，也不該 scale。反過來，估計0.15但 CI 很寬，可能值得再做更大 test，而不是直接判定無效。

好的 experiment report 應分開回答：有沒有 effect 證據？effect 多大？不確定性多高？economic value 是否支持 implementation？Statistical significance 是證據，不是自動 go/no-go rule。
paragraphs.ja:
A/B testでstatistical significanceが出ても、business decisionとして価値があるとは限りません。有意差は観測差がrandom sampling variationだけでは説明しにくいことを示しますが、effectが経済的に十分大きいかは別問題です。

例えば200万人でtestし、treatment conversion 1.02％、control 1.00％なら、sampleが大きいため0.02pt差でもsignificantになる可能性があります。しかし10万人当たり追加conversionは20件です。価値はrevenue、margin、campaign cost、operational complexityで決まります。

そのためp-valueとeffect sizeを一緒に報告します。tiny effectでも精密に推定されれば有意になりますし、小sampleのmoderate effectはnoiseのため有意にならないことがあります。not significantはno effectと同義ではなく、significantもimportantと同義ではありません。

confidence intervalはuncertaintyとmagnitudeを同時に示します。interval全体がcostをcoverできないほど小さければ、統計的にcredibleでもeconomically unattractiveです。

business valueはscaleにも依存します。小さいeffectでも数千万人へ低costで適用できれば価値があり、couponやcall centerなど一人当たりcostが高ければ魅力は下がります。重要なのはexpected incremental profitです。

heterogeneityも確認します。overall effectが小さくても一部segmentでは大きい場合があります。ただし大量のsubgroupを事後探索するとmisleading patternを見つけやすいため注意が必要です。

experiment前にminimum detectable effectとminimum economically meaningful effectを分けて定義するとよいでしょう。前者は何を検出できるか、後者は何なら実行価値があるかです。

例えば採算上0.10pt必要なのにestimateが0.03ptなら、非常にsignificantでもscaleしない判断があり得ます。逆に0.15ptでもCIが広ければ追加testが適切かもしれません。

報告ではevidence、effect size、uncertainty、economic valueを分けて説明し、p-valueを自動的なgo/no-go ruleにしないことが重要です。

vocabulary.usage: Statistical significance is not the same as business value.
Use a confidence interval to show uncertainty.
Optimize incremental profit, not significance alone.
A small effect can matter at scale.
Report a plausible range of effects.
Include implementation cost in the decision.

business.term: Significant does not automatically mean economically meaningful.
business.explanation: 區分統計證據與商業價值。

sources: A/B testing, effect size, confidence intervals, minimum meaningful effect, and campaign economics.
